382YE Autumn Equinox winds of fortune.d: Dawn and the Golden Axe seized Bittershore and Galath Fields in Ossium, along with the town of Lomaa and the Crawling Depths mithril mine. The Highborn faced the ruinous cost of committing their nation against the vallorn. Other winds covered orc affairs, League city politics, troubles with feni in Hahnmark and the Mournwold, Mazo i Zabala i Erigo's call to raid Grendel, army opportunities for four nations, a road survey, Phaleron's return and an orphanage for the Mournwold. Eight Synod mandates were upheld, though two linked to the Temple of the Winds stalled after the Druj destroyed it in Peregro. The Conclave added Sutannir's Promise to Imperial lore.

n.Dawn: Dawn's armies, alongside the Golden Axe, captured Bittershore and Galath Fields in Ossium, while its troubadours named champions of virtue and the nation faced fundamental choices about its armies.
n.Druj: The Druj lost Bittershore and Galath Fields in Ossium to Imperial attack, but their destruction of the Temple of the Winds in Peregro stalled two Synod mandates.
n.Grendel: The Grendel appeared on the doorstep of Sarvos and were the subject of Mazo i Zabala i Erigo's call for the Freeborn to raid them and free their slaves, with the orcs of the Broken Shore described as overconfident and over-extended.
n.Highguard: The Highborn faced the ruinous cost of committing their entire nation against the vallorn, with Lilith of the Chantry's mandate setting citizens on radical pilgrimages along the trods and another urging virtuous trade in white granite.
n.Imperial Orcs: Irontide Lok's mandate means the Imperial Orcs will begin to build a new martial nation in Skarsind, and the nation was also tagged in the season's orc affairs report.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the former Jotun thralls living in the Mournwold are among the orc groups covered by the orc affairs report.
n.Navarr: Navarr was concerned with developments among the orcs of the Great Forest and with the state of the trods and the ebb and flow of the war against the vallorn.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn raised the banner of the Burning Falcon, and Mazo i Zabala i Erigo called on them to raid Grendel and liberate its slaves, while a chill wind quieted the disruption in Segura.
n.The League: The League's cities faced the war against bite, renewed arguments over Empress Giselle's resting place, building work in Holberg and the arrival of the Grendel at Sarvos.
n.The Marches: The Marches faced feni troubles in the Mournwold, a call to build an orphanage for Mournwold orphans, army choices, developments among the former thralls, and a mandate to lay the ghosts of the Greensward to rest.
n.Thule: Developments with the Thule were covered in the orc affairs report, flagged for the Senate's attention.
n.Urizen: Urizen saw the Academy leave Canterspire, the return of the eternal Phaleron, and its mandate to restore the Temple of the Winds stalled by the temple's destruction in Peregro.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe fought alongside Dawn to capture two regions of Ossium, and Varushka was tagged in the orc affairs report and in a road survey that cited the Roads of Karsk as a success.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark faced a feni band raising trouble in Hahnmark, restated its commitment to heroism in its armies, and appeared in the orc affairs report, the road survey and talk of joining the Northern trade network.

t.Astolat: The Academy, the foremost school for future Imperial heroes, decided to leave Canterspire for a new home in Astolat.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Mazo i Zabala i Erigo's call to raid Grendel spread like wildfire along the Imperial coast of the Bay of Catazar.
t.Hahnmark: One of two troublesome feni bands headed north into Hahnmark, and the situation appeared to be coming to a head.
t.Holberg: Significant building work in Holberg featured among the season's League urban events.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Kallavesa is not named on this page and is touched only through Wintermark's wider concerns.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the Roads of Karsk were cited as a success in the civil service's road-building survey.
t.Morrow: The Druj destruction of the Temple of the Winds in Peregro left two Synod mandates without immediate effect until the region is retaken and the temple completed.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold saw a feni band causing trouble, the involvement of Alderly's mysterious inhabitants, a call for an orphanage for its orphans, developments among the former Jotun thralls, and a mandate to lay the Greensward's ghosts to rest.
t.Ossium: Dawn and the Golden Axe captured Bittershore and Galath Fields, along with the town of Lomaa and the Crawling Depths mithril mine, and made first contact with the territory's inhabitants.
t.Sarvos: The Grendel turned up on the doorstep of Sarvos this season.
t.Segura: A chill wind, raised by the Winds of Magic, swept across Segura, quieting the disruption there and stealing its magic.

r.Morrow/Peregro: The Temple of the Winds was destroyed by the Druj; if Peregro is liberated before the Summer Solstice 383YE, construction can begin again from scratch without a new commission or Senate motion.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: The mysterious inhabitants of Alderly became involved in the escalating trouble with the feni.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Albert Fugglestone-Copperhill's mandate means the ghosts haunting the ruins of Overton will be laid to rest.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Bittershore was captured from the Druj by the armies of Dawn and the Golden Axe.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: Galath Fields was captured from the Druj by the armies of Dawn and the Golden Axe.

382YE Autumn Equinox winds of war.d: In Morrow, some 45,000 Druj overwhelmed three Highborn armies, taking Peregro and Caeli and destroying the Halls of Knowledge, the Glorious Fountain, the Gardens of Morrow, the Temple of the Winds and the central Heliopticon tower. They were held only at Operus, and four thousand Highborn were lost. After Imperial forces withdrew, the Jotun took all of Sermersuaq except the Thule-held Silver Peaks, while the recently dead rose there. In Kahraman, Marcher and Navarr armies expelled the Jotun into Reinos. A Grendel armada demanded 400 thrones to spare the southern coast. Four Dawnish armies crossed the Golden Causeway and, with Varushka's Golden Axe, conquered Bittershore and the Galath Fields, capturing Lomaa and its Crawling Depths mithril mine.

n.Dawn: Dawn's four armies crossed the Golden Causeway from Semmerholm into the Mallum. They routed a Druj levy of some twenty thousand on the Galath Fields for minimal losses and helped seize Lomaa and its mithril mine.
n.Druj: The Druj conquered Peregro and Caeli in Morrow and destroyed many Urizen treasures. In Ossium, however, the Bone Serpent clan was broken, losing Bittershore, the Galath Fields, Lomaa and the Crawling Depths to the Empire.
n.Grendel: The Salt Lords anchored a vast armada off Sarvos and delivered an ultimatum: pay four hundred thrones or see a southern territory sacked after the Autumn Equinox.
n.Highguard: The Highborn armies (the Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus) were outnumbered and driven back in Morrow, losing four thousand soldiers before holding at Operus. Necropolis and Reikos were named among the coastal lands the Grendel threatened.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc captains marched across the Golden Causeway with the Dawnish host. Jotun raiders began pressing into Pakaanan's Pass in Skarsind shortly before the equinox.
n.Jotun: The Jotun took all of Sermersuaq save the Silver Peaks, offering the Winterfolk the Choice and fighting the risen dead, but they were driven entirely out of Kahraman back into Reinos.
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step, nearly doubled by Imperial captains, helped expel the Jotun from Kahraman. The Eternal Cathan Canae's frozen citadel was key to holding Operus in Morrow.
n.The Brass Coast: Kahraman was wholly recovered, though the town of Damata and its walls were badly damaged. The Grendel armada swept past the Coast, crushing Freeborn ships that came too close.
n.The League: Sarvos lay under the shadow of the Grendel armada, and its garrison at Our Lady of Pride stood watch as many citizens fled. League captains also joined the invasion of the Mallum.
n.The Marches: The Drakes and Strong Reeds, reinforced by many Imperial captains, led the campaign that drove the Jotun out of Kahraman. Marcher captains also marched with Dawn into Ossium.
n.Thule: Honouring the recent peace, Thule magicians laid healing Spring magic over Sermersuaq while keeping the Silver Peaks. They allowed the escaping mithril miners free passage without toll.
n.Urizen: Urizen suffered grievously: the Halls of Knowledge, the Glorious Fountain, the Temple of the Winds and the central Heliopticon tower were lost. With two Morrow regions fallen, the nation can no longer properly support its armies.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe marched south from Karsk to join Dawn, helping capture Lomaa. Moresvah families offered to work the newly seized Crawling Depths mithril mine.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark lost Sermersuaq entirely to the Jotun, and its fallen heroes rose as ravening dead. Jotun raiders then began pressing into Northspires, Bruckland and Skymark.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: some Imperial forces withdrew from Sermersuaq as far as Astolat, the Strong Reeds marched west from it, and the Academy chose to relocate there.
t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel armada controlled the Bay, able to strike any Imperial territory along its shores unless tribute was paid.
t.Feroz: Fisherfolk and corsairs sighted the passing armada, and Feroz was named among the rich territories the Grendel threatened to sack.
t.Hahnmark: Refugees fled into Hahnmark from Sermersuaq, and Jotun raiders began pressing into Northspires and Bruckland.
t.Kahraman: After a season of back-and-forth fighting the Jotun were expelled entirely. The Damatian Cliffs were reclaimed, but the white granite quarry must be reallocated by the Senate.
t.Kallavesa: Imperial forces withdrew into Kallavesa from Sermersuaq, and Jotun raiders began pressing into Skymark.
t.Karsk: The Golden Axe marched south from Karsk along the Semmerlak to invade Ossium, and Moresvah families offered to work the captured mithril mine.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: former bandits from the heights between Kahraman and Liathaven fought for the Jotun under the firebird banner.
t.Madruga: The Drakes marched from Madruga to Kahraman, refugees from Rojota passed through, and the territory was named as a possible Grendel target.
t.Morrow: The Druj conquered Peregro and Caeli and gained a foothold in Operus, destroying great works across the east. One more lost region would hand Morrow to the Druj.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: some Imperial forces withdrawing from Sermersuaq went south into the Mournwold.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: named among the territories the Grendel threatened to sack.
t.Ossium: Dawn and Varushka conquered Bittershore and the Galath Fields and pushed into the Bonewood. They broke the Bone Serpent clan and seized Lomaa and its mithril mine.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov may know more about the Thule sheltering the escaped mithril miners.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: named among the territories the Grendel threatened to sack.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: veterans of the Reikos campaign recognised the far heavier Druj miasma in Ossium.
t.Reinos: The defeated Jotun were driven out of Kahraman back into Reinos, with a kirkja rearguard at the Monachil Gorge on the border.
t.Sarvos: The Grendel armada anchored off Sarvos and its emissary delivered the tribute ultimatum at the docks. Many citizens fled while others armed themselves.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Rojota sought shelter in Cerevado, welcomed by its gambling houses while their coin lasted.
t.Semmerholm: The Dawnish armies gathered at Lacre and Lacuve and marched across the Golden Causeway from Semmerholm into the Mallum.
t.Sermersuaq: The whole territory fell to orcs: the Jotun hold everything except the Thule-held Silver Peaks. The recently dead rose to attack orc and human alike.
t.Skarsind: Jotun raiders began pressing into Pakaanan's Pass, while the escaping miners' caravan was granted passage through Crow's Ridge towards Torfast.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: named among the territories the Grendel might strike, and Hadrian of Apulian's example is cited.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: some Sarvosan citizens fled as far as Tassato.
t.The Semmerlak: The Golden Causeway rose across the Semmerlak, carrying the Dawnish host into the Mallum in a single day, and red pillars remain on the far shore to recall it.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: scholars from Therunin once travelled the trod the Druj now used to invade Morrow.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step came down past Fort Braydon from Upwold, joined by the garrison there.
t.Zenith: The Druj launched their invasion of Morrow from Proceris and Clypion, and a major conjunction opens in Lustri along their supply lines.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: Mentioned in passing: rumour held that the Grendel might sail to Oran to sack the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull.
r.Hahnmark/Bruckland: Jotun raiders began pressing into Bruckland three weeks before the equinox.
r.Hahnmark/Northspires: Jotun raiders began pressing into Northspires three weeks before the equinox.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Jotun captured the town of Rojota, causing many to flee, before being driven out and hounded across Gambit's plains.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: A Dawnish-raised glacial citadel defended Briante and its mithril mine against a determined Jotun siege before the decisive Imperial push.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Serra Damata was freed entirely, though Damata town and its walls were badly damaged. A conjunction opens at the Monachil Gorge against the Jotun rearguard.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: Jotun raiders began pressing into Skymark three weeks before the equinox.
r.Karsk/Lestasny: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Axe marched south out of Lestasny along the Semmerlak.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: Mentioned in passing: Malinov, Sloev and Pravin families of Moresvah offered to help work the Crawling Depths mine.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Mentioned in passing: rumour suggested the armada might rescue Innevia, captured by the Drakes during Free Landing's liberation.
r.Morrow/Altis: Mentioned in passing: professors and librarians fled west to Altis from the burning Halls of Knowledge.
r.Morrow/Caeli: Caeli fell to the Druj: the Seat of the Arbiter, its library and stele were destroyed, the Gardens of Morrow burned and the central Heliopticon tower lost.
r.Morrow/Operus: The Highborn finally held the Druj at Operus around the Cathan Canae citadel, though the orcs took a few spires on its south-eastern edge.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Peregro fell to the Druj, who destroyed the Glorious Fountain, the Temple of the Winds and the Halls of Knowledge.
r.Morrow/Ravion: Mentioned in passing: Druj scouts clashed with the Seventh Wave as far west as Ravion.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: The region where the Golden Causeway lands was conquered by Dawn and Varushka. They found Sand Fisher villages and enslaved humans and orcs under Bone Serpent rule.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Imperial advance pushed only a short way into this hostile northern forest, where scouts glimpsed pale, thirsty figures among the pines.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: Dawn crushed a Druj levy here and the Empire captured Lomaa, the Bone Serpent seat, with its mithril mine. The Bleak Vein regio conjunction lies nearby.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: scouts guessed the land beyond the Bonewood is Sküld's vallorn-haunted southern forest.
r.Sarvos/Foracci: Mentioned in passing: many Sarvosans fled to Foracci, whose inns did their best business in a decade.
r.Sarvos/Riposi: Mentioned in passing: many Sarvosans fled to Riposi, filling its inns.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Rojota sought refuge in Cerevado's gambling houses and paradors.
r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: The Dawnish host gathered at Lacuve and Lacre, where the white granite gate roused the Golden Causeway to launch the invasion.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The Jotun swept through East Floes, completing their conquest.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Sealtoq fell under Jotun control as part of the conquest of all Sermersuaq outside the Silver Peaks.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule kept the Silver Peaks and sheltered the escaping mithril miners as guests.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The Jotun overran Suaq Fount and took the Pride of Ikka's Tears mine, though its miners escaped east with the season's mithril.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Tens of thousands of Jotun swept through the Suaq Wastes, completing their conquest.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Mentioned in passing: the Thule let the miners' caravan pass through to Crow's Ridge without toll.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Jotun raiders began pressing into Pakaanan's Pass three weeks before the equinox.
r.Skarsind/Solvihill: Mentioned in passing: the miners' caravan was bound via Crow's Ridge for Torfast.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Mentioned in passing: the Heliopticon's magicians were perhaps inspired by Hadrian of Apulian's example.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Druj forces pushed north from Clypion into Caeli. Clypion was the former site of the Halls of Knowledge before they moved to Morrow.
r.Zenith/Lustri: A major conjunction opens near the ruined Spire of Twisting Shadows, where the Druj supply lines run back to the Mallum.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Some twenty thousand Druj marched north from Proceris along the trod into Peregro, launching the invasion of Morrow.

A blessing in disguise.d: Lilith of the Chantry carried the mandate across Highguard, and thousands prepared to walk the trods. The civil service estimated that every Highborn farm and business would lose 72 rings of income and every military unit two ranks, with the penalties lasting at least ten years. Any nation except Highguard could pass a mandate, with 50 liao (25 for Navarr and Urizen), to offer pilgrims food, shelter and protection. Each supporting nation would take half the penalty, and each additional nation would shorten the adjustment period, down to one season with eight or more. The planned fourth Highborn army had to be abandoned, but veterans could enlarge one existing army for 100 mithril and 25 thrones if the Senate approved. All options were valid only at the Autumn Equinox 382YE.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but the page notes Highborn armies recently bled defending Urizeni lands in Zenith and Morrow.
n.Highguard: Highborn citizens set out on a vast pilgrimage at a ruinous projected cost of 72 rings per farm and business and two ranks per military unit, and their planned fourth army was abandoned. They could instead enlarge an existing army with eager veterans if the Senate approved it that season.
n.Navarr: Navarr, who understand the vallorn and migratory life better than anyone, could endorse the support mandate for only 25 liao, with wayhouses welcoming the pilgrims, at the cost of 36 rings per farm and business and one rank per military unit.
n.Urizen: Urizen, grateful for Highborn armies bleeding in defence of Zenith and Morrow, could endorse the support mandate for only 25 liao, with stargazers finding safe routes for pilgrims, at the cost of 36 rings per farm and business and one rank per military unit.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark, like any non-Highborn nation, could pass the support mandate, and its halls are suggested as places that might take pilgrims in and offer them seats by the fire.

t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is cited as a land where Highborn armies recently bled defending Urizen, which inclines some Urizeni to support the pilgrims.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is cited as a land where Highborn armies recently bled in defence of Urizen.

Allocate Crawling Depths.d: The motion assigned the Crawling Depths, a mithril mine in Ossium, as an Imperial Bourse seat, and it passed. As a result the position is Imperial, and any Imperial citizen is eligible to hold the associated title. The page notes that this allocation is permanent: even once Ossium is conquered and assigned to an Imperial nation, the Crawling Depths will remain an Imperial position, and there will be no further opportunity to allocate it to that nation or any other.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj held Ossium when the Senate allocated the Crawling Depths there as an Imperial Bourse seat; they are not otherwise named.

t.Ossium: The mithril mine of the Crawling Depths in Ossium was made an Imperial Bourse seat, and it will stay Imperial even if Ossium is conquered and given to an Imperial nation.

Chilled to the bone.d: After defeating a force of pressed Druj farmers on the Galath Fields, Imperial forces spread across Ossium without maps. At Lomaa, seat of the Bone Serpent clan, the Dawnish took the Crawling Depths and freed about five hundred slaves born underground. The mine produces 14 wains of mithril a season; a 300-throne Senate commission taking two seasons would double that, and the Senate may allocate it as Imperial or national. The trapped weirwood hall of the Bitter Vats produces herbs and Oil of Blackthorn, a spoil of war for the Military Council to assign. The hopeless Sand Fishers orcs and the calculating Varushkan-like townsfolk of Ketsov both submitted to Imperial rule.

n.Druj: The Druj were caught completely unprepared, with their elite troops absent and only pressed farmers and labourers in the field. The Bone Serpent clan lost its clan seat at Lomaa, its mithril mine and its poison workshop, and Ketsov's Druj-allied leaders fled east with what wealth they could carry.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: soldiers who fought in the Reikos campaign are noted as having seen slaves before, though none had seen people reduced to the state of the Crawling Depths slaves.

t.Ossium: Imperial forces seized much of Ossium, including the Crawling Depths and the Bitter Vats at Lomaa. Without maps, though, they struggled to work out exactly what they had conquered, and the Sand Fishers and Ketsovs waited to learn who would now rule them.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: veterans of the Reikos campaign are cited as having encountered slaves there before.
t.The Semmerlak: The Sand Fishers fish, catch crabs and hunt eels in the lake's shallow waters. Its violent storms and turbulent river leave them feeling unable to flee Druj rule, and their oral history says they once controlled the lands all round it.

r.Ossium/Bittershore: The Bittershore was where the Empire first met the Sand Fishers. Bone Snake symbols are painted everywhere there to mark the clan's ownership, and the Sand Fishers quietly keep their sashes in case the Druj return.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: The Empire won a great battle here against a far larger force of conscripted Druj labourers. Control of the Bitter Vats depends on holding the region, and would be lost if the Druj reconquered it.

Commission report on Morrow evacuation.d: Proposed by the senator for Morrow and seconded by the senator for Spiral, this Autumn 382YE motion asked the Imperial Civil Service to investigate whether evacuating the civilian population of Morrow was feasible and, if so, to set out how it could be done. The motion passed. The Civil Service was expected to present its findings at the Winter Solstice 382YE. The motion itself commissioned only a report; it did not order or begin any evacuation.

n.Urizen: Urizen's senator for Morrow proposed the motion, seeking a civil service study into how the nation's civilians in that territory might be evacuated.

t.Morrow: Morrow's civilians were the subject of the commissioned study, with the civil service tasked to find possible evacuation routes and report back at the Winter Solstice 382YE.

Construct Drusila's Obelus.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave, Lukash announced the commission of a sinecure named Drusilla's Obelus in the Morass region of Holberg. The project used standard costs of 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, and would take three months to complete. Lukash Biessek von Temeschwar provided the full weirwood and crowns after the Autumn equinox 382YE. Once complete, the sinecure creates an Imperial title, Drusilla's Obelus, which yields 18 drams of bladeroot per season. The title is to be held for life and allocated by auction through the Bourse.

n.The League: A new League landmark was commissioned in Holberg, and Lukash Biessek von Temeschwar funded it in full to create a lifetime title producing bladeroot.

t.Holberg: Holberg was to gain Drusilla's Obelus, a sinecure whose holder receives 18 drams of bladeroot each season.

r.Holberg/The Morass: The Morass was chosen as the site of Drusilla's Obelus, which would take three months to build once its weirwood and crowns were supplied.

Construct Eastern Spring Farm.d: Using an Imperial Orc Wayleave, Palerictus Krunk announced in Autumn 382YE the construction of a sinecure in the east of Skarsind, intended for the betterment of spring ritualists within the Imperial Orc nation. The commission used standard costs, though its size was not specified. After the Autumn Equinox, Palerictus Krunk provided 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns towards the work. When complete, the sinecure will create a new Imperial title, the Farmer of Eastern Spring Farm.

n.Imperial Orcs: An Imperial Orc wayleave was used to commission a sinecure meant to support the nation's spring ritualists, funded with mithril and crowns from Palerictus Krunk.

t.Skarsind: The sinecure is to be built in the east of Skarsind, and once complete it will establish the title Farmer of Eastern Spring Farm there.

Construct First Voice Glade.d: Idwyn Splitroot, acting as proxy for Matt Twisted Tree, used an Imperial Wayleave in Autumn 382YE to announce a herb garden sinecure in Miaren. Its inscription honours Gerallt the bard, First Voice of the Navarr nation, who died at Return, and records that the bards of Navarr gather at his Glade. The title is appointed by the Navarr Senators and revocable by the Navarr National Assembly. The sinecure used standard costs, though its size was not specified. Nemae provided 20 weirwood and 40 crowns after the Autumn Equinox. The completed work created a new Imperial title, Dean of the First Voice Glade.

n.Navarr: Navarr gained a memorial glade honouring its fallen First Voice Gerallt and a new title, Dean of the First Voice Glade, appointed by its Senators and answerable to its National Assembly.

t.Miaren: First Voice Glade, a herb garden sinecure and gathering place for the bards of Navarr, was raised in Miaren.

Construct Good Leaf Gardens.d: Proposed by Miaren and seconded by Mitwold, the motion arose from a suggestion by Morgan of Brock Bottom Steading following a statement of principle by Corey Brackensong. The accompanying mandate was raised in the Navarr National Assembly, and Brat Umbral Path provided the liao to enact it, allowing the folly to operate as a sinecure. The commission used non-standard costs of 15 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns, taking three months to complete. William Talbot provided the weirwood and crowns after the Autumn Equinox 382YE. Its completion creates a new Imperial title, a national position in the Marches called Steward of Good Leaf Gardens.

n.Navarr: The Navarr, through their National Assembly mandate and liao from Brat Umbral Path, offered their herbs to the Marches as thanks for Marcher support in the fight against the vallorn.
n.The Marches: The Marches gained Good Leaf Gardens, stocked with Navarri herbs, and a new national title, Steward of Good Leaf Gardens, with William Talbot providing the weirwood and crowns to build it.

t.Upwold: Good Leaf Gardens was commissioned as a wayhouse in Upwold, where it serves as a sinecure sharing Navarri herbs with the Marches.

Construct Jarmish Jewellers.d: Proposed by Temeschwar and seconded by Kahraman, the motion would have commissioned a fortified premises in Seren for the Kobarid family of Jarm to sell glazamy neba, their magical jewellery, to Imperial customers, following an offer by the Jarmish Magician-Prince Matvei Kobarid. It was to be self-funded at a non-standard cost of 8 wains of white granite, 4 wains of mithril and 24 crowns, taking three months to complete. The resulting Imperial title, a liaison appointed by open auction on the Bourse, would have been able to buy up to three pieces of rare jewellery each season at a bargain price. No progress was made, and the motion was abrogated at the Winter Solstice 382YE.

n.Navarr: The Navarr territory of Miaren was to host a Jarmish jewellery exchange, giving Imperial buyers access to Kobarid magical jewellery, but the project was abrogated before construction began.

t.Miaren: Seren in Miaren was chosen as the site for a fortified Jarmish Star Jewellery exchange run by the Kobarid family, but the commission was abrogated at the Winter Solstice 382YE with no progress made.

Construct Sarcombe Metal Market.d: Proposed by the Senator for Mournwold and seconded by Bregasland, the motion sought a self-funded ministry at Sarcombe whose holder, the Keeper of Metal, would be appointed annually by agreement of the Marcher Senators and could be revoked by the Marcher assembly. The commission used standard costs. After the Autumn Equinox 382YE, Landon of Longridge provided 20 wains of mithril and 5 Thrones to complete it. The finished ministry created an Imperial title, Master of Sarcombe Metal Market, and is expected to help secure the economic stability of the market town of Sarcombe.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a metal-trading ministry under its own control. The Marcher Senators agree its holder each year, and the Marcher assembly can revoke the appointment.

t.Mournwold: The ministry was built in the market town of Sarcombe, where it is expected to help secure the town's economic stability.

Construct Sarcombe Register.d: Proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Feroz, the motion sought to take up the opportunity to build the Sarcombe Register in the newly established market town of Sarcombe. The folly would have allowed orphans to be registered with the aim of finding them new families, and would have created the position of Custodian of the Registry, appointed for life by the Marcher senators and revocable by the Marcher Assembly. The motion failed, so the folly was not commissioned and no Custodian was created.

n.The Marches: The Marches lost a proposed folly that would have helped find families for orphans, along with a new Custodian of the Registry title that Marcher senators would have appointed and the Marcher Assembly could have revoked.

t.Mournwold: The orphan registry planned for the new market town of Sarcombe in the Mournwold was not built after the motion failed.

Construct Tower of the Wheel.d: Commissioned in Autumn 382YE as an opportunity based on Richard of Holberg's designs, the Tower of the Wheel used non-standard costs: 10 wains of weirwood plus 20 crowns of labour and additional materials, taking three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 382YE, Vitore provided 400 rings and the 10 wains of weirwood. When complete, the sinecure will create a new Imperial title, the Watcher of the Wheel, whose holder can each season harvest and process magically infused plants yielding one portion each of warm ashes, vital honey, crystal fire and heart's blood.

n.The League: A League territory is set to gain a new mana-producing sinecure and an Imperial title, the Watcher of the Wheel, built to designs by Richard of Holberg and funded with materials provided by Vitore.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the tower's designer is named as Richard of Holberg.
t.Tassato: Tassato is the site of the Tower of the Wheel, where the Watcher of the Wheel will harvest magically infused plants each season for warm ashes, vital honey, crystal fire and heart's blood once the three-month construction is complete.

Construct Wintermark beacons.d: The motion arose from a civil service proposal and was to be funded entirely by Tyr Brenna of Hendall Hearth. The commission used non-standard costs: 40 wains of white granite, 40 wains of weirwood and 160 crowns in labour, taking six months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox, Hengest Dun provided the 40 wains of weirwood, 40 wains of white granite and 20 thrones. Once complete, the beacons would allow military unit commanders to defend Kallavesa and Hahnmark and to offer resistance to invading armies.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's own senators and a Wintermark hearth championed and funded the beacons. Once built, they would let military unit commanders help defend two of the nation's territories against invasion.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's senator proposed the motion. The territory was to gain a network of beacons and watchtowers that, once complete, would let military unit commanders resist invading armies there.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's senator seconded the motion, and the territory was to receive beacons and watchtowers that would let military unit commanders defend it against invaders.

Disburse funds to Grendel raiders.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by the senator for Morrow, the motion responded to demands the Grendel made before the Autumn Equinox. It proposed paying the Grendel in return for their promise not to invade or sack Imperial territories bordering the Bay of Catazar for the season. The motion passed with the sum set at 300 thrones, and the money was disbursed to the senator for Holberg to deliver.

n.Grendel: The Grendel's demands were met with a payment of 300 thrones, given in return for their promise not to invade or sack Imperial territories on the Bay of Catazar this season.

t.Bay of Catazar: The payment was meant to secure the Imperial territories around the Bay against Grendel invasion or sacking for the season.

Fortify Coursmouth.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Casinea and seconded by the senator for Necropolis. It used standard costs: 80 wains of white granite, 160 crowns in labour, a year to build and 10 Thrones in upkeep. Lieselotte van Holberg supplied 24 wains of granite and 48 crowns after the Autumn Equinox 382YE, and the project was targeted by The Immaculate Architect. Imperatrix Lisabetta added 30 wains and 10 Thrones after the Winter Solstice. The Silent Sentinel opportunity effectively contributed a further 16 wains and 32 crowns. Ehud of Reumah's Redoubt gave the final 10 wains after the Spring Equinox 383YE. The finished fortification was named Reumah's Rest.

n.Highguard: Highguard senators for Casinea and Necropolis proposed and seconded the work. Highborn donors helped see it through, and it left the nation with a new fortification guarding the Necropolis coast.

t.Necropolis: Necropolis gained Reumah's Rest, a new fortification on its coast, after its own senator seconded the motion.

r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Coursmouth became the site of Reumah's Rest, a white granite fortification built along its coastline.

Fortify Morajasse.d: The commission passed at 90 thrones and used standard costs: 80 wains of white granite, 20 thrones in labour, a year to build and 10 thrones upkeep. Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza supplied 24 wains and 6 thrones after the Autumn Equinox 382YE. The Silent Sentinel opportunity effectively provided another 16 wains and 4 thrones, and the work was also targeted by The Immaculate Architect. Imperatrix Lisabetta gave 20 wains and 5 thrones after the Winter Solstice and a further 5 thrones after the Spring Equinox 383YE. Landon of Longridge provided the last 20 wains. A new fortification now stands at Morajasse.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast's senator for Feroz proposed the motion, and Brass Coast lands gained a new fortification at Morajasse, which Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza helped to fund.

t.Feroz: Feroz gained a new fortification at Morajasse, which strengthens the territory's defences and carries an upkeep of 10 thrones.

r.Feroz/Morajasse: A new fortification was built at Morajasse, completed with white granite and money gathered from several donors.

Improve Our Lady of Pride.d: The commission, raised by the Imperial Master of Works, used standard costs of 100 wains of White Granite and 200 crowns of labour, taking a year to complete. It would benefit from vigilant citizens if materials were provided before the Winter Solstice. Contributions came from Gancio (30 wains and 7 thrones 4 crowns), the Silent Sentinel opportunity (effectively 20 wains and 40 crowns), Landon of Longridge (25 wains), Imperatrix Lisabetta (6 thrones 2 crowns, plus 50 crowns given on her behalf by Severin Teyhard von Holberg) and Lieselotte van Holberg (25 wains), across seasons up to Summer 383YE. On completion the fortification's effective strength would rise to 6,000.

n.The League: League citizens, including Imperatrix Lisabetta, Lieselotte van Holberg and Severin Teyhard von Holberg, supplied much of the granite and money to strengthen a key fortification in their own territory.

t.Sarvos: Our Lady of Pride in Sarvos was to be enlarged to an effective strength of 6,000, bolstering the territory's defences once the year-long work was finished.

In the end everything collides.d: Yevgeni Katzev's treaty guaranteed Thule holdings in the Silver Peaks and Lestazny and ceded Crow's Ridge, which a Thule army occupied without bloodshed. The Thule agreed to ransom Imperial slaves, with talks due at the Winter Solstice, and Grand Warlock Fljajokull was to visit Anvil to discuss military aid in Ossium. The Thule rejected the Senate's claim to Sungold Pass, though both sides agreed not to build until it is settled. The Thule demanded reparations after the hungry dead in Sermersuaq killed twenty orcs. Up to a hundred Great Forest orcs, along with a few briars, joined Navarr stridings. A Grendel envoy sought to ransom Commander Innevia.

n.Druj: The Thule agreed in principle to an alliance against the Druj, promising strategic information, and sent a grand warlock to discuss direct military aid against them in Ossium.
n.Grendel: Grendel privateers continued raiding in the Bay of Catazar, while an emissary of Salt Lord Moorvain of Vorlach headed to Anvil to negotiate the ransom of Commander Innevia and her surrendered troops.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the many Highborn becoming pilgrims after Highguard's grand sacrifice are contrasted with the Great Forest orcs walking the trods.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs lost Crow's Ridge in Skarsind to the Thule under the treaty, and their few settlers there moved south. Some resented it, but most felt they would not complain when Wintermark and Varushka had also given up land.
n.Jotun: The former Jotun thralls in the Mournwold went on farming and paying taxes, though a murder case and Hap the Soft's dismissal of the magistrates caused some unease.
n.Navarr: At the invitation of the Navarr National Assembly, perhaps a hundred Great Forest orcs and a few briars joined Navarr stridings on the trods. Meanwhile, Navarr artisans captured by the Thule remained a sticking point in the slave negotiations.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: following Eska Crowspeaker's mandate, well-meaning folk from the Brass Coast travelled to the Mourn to help thralls, who insisted they were farmers, not slaves.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel armada off Sarvos is noted, and well-meaning citizens of Tassato went to offer succour to the Mournwold thralls.
n.The Marches: Anna Pernn's statement led thralls to be advised to take disputes to the Mournwold senator, who has no power to resolve criminal cases. Some Mournwolders still decried the Empire's "appeasement" of the orcs.
n.Thule: The Thule gained Crow's Ridge and agreed to ransom Imperial slaves and share intelligence on the Druj. They also disputed the Empire's claim to Sungold Pass and demanded reparations for orcs killed by the hungry dead in Sermersuaq.
n.Varushka: Varushkan soldiers watched over Sungold Pass after the Senate claimed it for Opascari and faced a Thule force across the pass. Varushka is also among the nations that ceded land to the Thule.
n.Wintermark: The treaty confirmed Thule control of the Silver Peaks, and the last Wintermark halls in Crow's Ridge had already been abandoned. The hungry dead in Sermersuaq provoked Thule outrage and a demand for reparations.

t.Bay of Catazar: Independent Grendel privateers continued to harry merchant shipping in the bay, though Imperial magic proved more than a match for them.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is not named; it is touched only by the general news of Great Forest orcs joining Navarr stridings on the trods.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Vuk the Wolfeater, the senator for Karov, raised the Senate motion claiming Sungold Pass for the Empire.
t.Karsk: The treaty guaranteed Thule control of the land they hold in Lestazny. Runesmiths and artisans captured during the Thule occupation of Treji remained a contested part of the slave negotiations.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Commander Innevia and her Grendel troops surrendered to Will Talbot during clean-up operations in Madruga, and a ransom emissary is now coming.
t.Mournwold: The thralls in the Mournwold kept working their land despite tensions over a murder case and an influx of outsiders trying to help "escaped slaves". The status quo held, but their issues, especially with the Way, remained unresolved.
t.Ossium: A Thule grand warlock was due at Anvil to discuss with the Military Council possible direct Thule military aid against the Druj in Ossium.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov's orcs sent an army south to occupy Crow's Ridge and agreed to begin slave ransom talks at the Winter Solstice. Their embassy formally rejected the Imperial claim to Sungold Pass.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel armada off the coast of Sarvos is noted as already documented elsewhere.
t.Sermersuaq: The treaty guaranteed Thule control of their lands in the Silver Peaks, but the hungry dead rising in Sermersuaq killed Thule orcs, prompting a demand for reparations.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind lost Crow's Ridge to the Thule under the treaty, and the few Imperial Orc settlers there withdrew south.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: some well-meaning citizens of Tassato travelled to the Mourn to offer succour to the thralls.
t.Therunin: The news of the Navarr invitation reached the Great Forest orcs in Therunin, and the first of them joined stridings there. One band also began exploring the vallorn-infested Sweetglades.
t.Volodmartz: The Senate declared Sungold Pass and the Traveller part of Opascari, but the Thule disputed this, and the two forces now face each other across the pass.

r.Otkodov/Sküld: The Thule claimed that the Traveller lies partly in Kógur in Sküld and that Sungold Pass sits on their side of the mountain.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: The Thule army that took Crow's Ridge marched south from Urdur, and new garrisons now overlook the passes into Urdur.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The treaty guaranteed Thule control of the Silver Peaks, but the hungry dead attacked two patrols and a mining settlement there, killing twenty orcs.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Crow's Ridge was ceded to the Thule and occupied without bloodshed. They are now restoring Crow's Keep and garrisoning the passes north and west.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: A band of Great Forest orcs, apparently after receiving Vitality of Rushing Water, cautiously explored the vallorn in Sweetglades, unsettling the local steadings.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: The Senate asserted that Sungold Pass belongs to Opascari. Varushkan soldiers and a Thule force are now camped across the pass from each other while the dispute awaits negotiation.

It can't get much worse.d: On Friday, heroes could rescue Wintermark refugees fleeing the Jotun at Floes Descent in Skarsind. They could also strike Druj bands in Morrow while saving scholars who escaped the Halls of Knowledge, and raid fugitive House Martel nobles at Rookwood Estate in the Barrens. Saturday's opportunities included saving poisoned Highborn physicks in Operus, which would preserve the Valiant Pegasus's ability to Tend the Fallen. Others were slaying an oduli at Cascade Pass and ambushing Writhing Shadow ritualists, raiding green iron carriers and hunting another oduli in Ossium. Heroes could also attempt to break a fear miasma pillar in Bittershore and drive off Grendel marines landing at Orieni Villa and Glass Point Cove.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish could raid disgraced House Martel at Rookwood Estate and avenge the Gryphon's Pride knights ambushed by an oduli in Galath Fields. They also had House Chambrun's anointed scout Heloise Fletcher's discovery of a miasma pillar in Bittershore to act on.
n.Druj: Druj bands were rampaging across Morrow with poisons, Tortured Souls and an oduli, while in Ossium their ritualists, green iron convoys and fear miasma pillars were all exposed to Imperial strikes.
n.Grendel: Grendel moridun marines made sudden landings at Orieni Villa in Feroz and Glass Point Cove in Sarvos, seeking to loot a mana sinecure and disrupt the ilium trade unless driven off.
n.Highguard: Highborn defenders were being driven back in Morrow. Physicks of the Valiant Pegasus were pinned down and poisoned near Silver Light Tower, and their rescue would decide whether the army had enough healers to Tend the Fallen.
n.Imperial Orcs: Jotun warriors were pursuing refugees into Pakaanan's Pass in the orcs' new home of Skarsind, and defeating them would stop the Jotun scouting routes into Imperial Orc lands.
n.Jotun: A Jotun warband of Skjaldir and Ulvenwar pursued fleeing Wintermark refugees into Skarsind, offering them The Choice, and risked defeat if heroes intercepted it at Floes Descent.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr skirmishers were expected to want to help in Morrow, and the in-character tale shows Thorns from Peakedge guiding fleeing Urizeni students.
n.The Brass Coast: Grendel marines surrounded the Orieni Villa near Cazar, seat of the Broken Shore Bounty, threatening to deprive the Empire of the coming season's ilium.
n.The League: Grendel marines landed at Glass Point Cove in Sarvos to loot the mana sinecure, and League-held Holberg served as the base for spies who located the House Martel fugitives.
n.Urizen: Morrow was being ravaged by the Druj, with the Halls of Knowledge destroyed. Scattered scholars who might be rescued could form the foundation of a new centre of magical learning.
n.Varushka: Varushkan wardens tracked Druj convoys carrying green iron through the Bonewood, giving Varushka a chance to raid them at Wither Oak and Warden's Reach.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark heroes and refugees fleeing the Jotun invasion of Sermersuaq were being hunted in Floes Descent, and a rescue could save citizens who would otherwise not reach Anvil.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel armada had lingered in the Bay for over a month, and fast ships hidden far out in its waters launched landings on the Feroz and Sarvos coasts.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark heroes would already have been travelling to Casinea had their lands not been invaded.
t.Feroz: Grendel marines stormed and surrounded the Orieni Villa near Cazar, threatening the ilium supply of the Broken Shore Bounty.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: magistrates' spies slip across the border from Holberg into the Carmine Fields, which helped locate the House Martel fugitives.
t.Morrow: The Druj were rampaging through eastern Morrow, using poisons, Tortured Souls and an oduli. Five conjunctions offered chances to strike back and to save the physicks and scholars fleeing there.
t.Ossium: As the Golden Axe advanced into Ossium, conjunctions offered strikes against Writhing Shadow ritualists, green iron convoys, an oduli and a fear miasma pillar, all within the Druj miasma.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Highborn who suffered in Reikos recognise the Tortured Souls now seen in Morrow.
t.Sarvos: Grendel marines landed at Glass Point Cove and held the cliff tops, threatening to loot the mana sinecure's coming production and leave the Custodian with repair costs.
t.Sermersuaq: Jotun armies swept across Sermersuaq, burning halls and forcing refugees and Wintermark heroes to flee east into Skarsind.
t.Skarsind: Refugees from Sermersuaq fled into Skarsind with Jotun warriors in pursuit, and defeating the warband would stop a Jotun raiding force scouting the territory.
t.The Barrens: The militia could raid fugitive House Martel nobles at Rookwood Estate, and dead yeofolk bearing Barrens house heraldry had been seen among the Druj as Tortured Souls.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: fleeing scholars and students were heading north to Therunin's forests, and poisoned soldiers collapsed near its border with Morrow.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: dead Zenith mages appeared among the Druj as Tortured Souls, and refugees from Proceris told of Druj monsters.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Grendel marines besieged the Orieni Villa near Cazar. If they were not repulsed, no ilium would be acquired that season, though a larger haul might follow.
r.Morrow/Caeli: Druj bands hunted villagers and fleeing scholars across Caeli, and conjunctions to Iron Citadel Field, Meadow of Clouds and Cascade Pass offered chances to strike back and slay an oduli being escorted through its ruins.
r.Morrow/Operus: Chikad and hupul attackers pinned down poisoned Valiant Pegasus physicks near Silver Light Tower, where Druj orc mages had also been harrying the Granite Pillar.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Druj fighters criss-crossed Peregro hunting refugees and scholars, with conjunctions to Peakedge Road and Sulphur Vent, and some feared the oduli might be led to its hot springs.
r.Morrow/Ravion: Mentioned in passing: some speculated that the Druj might use the oduli in Ravion to repeat the rite that turned Proceris into swamp.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: An anointed Chambrun scout found a miasma pillar inland from Scarred Bay, which heroes could try to break through consecration or ritual.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: Writhing Shadow ritualists could be ambushed at Blood Spike Glade, and Druj convoys carrying green iron could be raided at Wither Oak and Warden's Reach.
r.Ossium/Galath Fields: An oduli and chikad ambushers that killed most of a band of Dawnish questing knights were last seen at Fangmoor Dwell, north of Lomaa.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Grendel marines and slaves landed at Glass Point Cove to loot the mana sinecure's coming season's production.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Refugees fled through the woods of Floes Descent with Jotun warriors close behind, and defeating them would deny the Jotun the chance to scout the pass.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Magistrate Karkovitch's militia could raid the Rookwood Estate to seize House Martel nobles wanted for murder, at the risk of alerting nearby Druj.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Proceris told of Druj monsters, and the valley had been turned into a foetid swamp by a Druj rite.

Oh so intricate.d: Autumn magic protecting Bay of Catazar traders faded, leaving fleets from Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen exposed to Grendel pirates. Citadels rose in several territories. Stars stayed missing over Semmerholm, the Barrens and Zenith, while penumbral veils covered Otkodov and several Imperial territories. The Icy Maw curse halved Segura's mana before fading. Meraud challenged magicians to feats of battle magic, Kimus sought volunteers for an experiment, and Leviathan arranged a meeting with the Lake Dwellers. Irra Harah renewed his bounty on two hearts. Sadogua, furious at the Druj, offered boons to Urizen and Highborn magicians and to Nicassia of the Citadel Guard.

n.Dawn: Semmerholm remained starless under a magnitude-fifty Night shroud, the Sherard Hunters raised Spring citadels in Axmure's forests, and Zadkiel de Coeurdefer still carries Irra Harah's bounty on his heart.
n.Druj: The Druj almost certainly maintain the star-shrouds over the Barrens, Zenith and Semmerholm, and their burning of the Halls of Knowledge enraged Sadogua, who broke his deal with the Ghulai and offered Imperial magicians power to devastate them.
n.Grendel: Grendel pirates had been thwarted by Autumn magic on the Bay of Catazar, but with that magic fading Imperial trading ships may again be at their mercy; a citadel was also raised in the hills and mountains of Spiral.
n.Highguard: Highborn fleets faced reduced trade as the protection on the Bay of Catazar faded, Necropolis lay under a penumbral veil, and Highborn magicians were offered Sadogua's boon of increased personal mana to use against the Druj.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven was among the lands starless in 381YE, and the Jotun presence in Sermersuaq may have caused the Lake Dwellers to rethink their attacks.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn fleets faced reduced trade, Madruga and Feroz lay under penumbral veils, a citadel rose in Kahraman, Segura suffered the Icy Maw curse, and Chiara i Zayden i Riqueza remains under Irra Harah's bounty.
n.The League: Fleets from Tassato and Sarvos faced reduced trade, Sarvos and Temeschwar lay under penumbral veils, and the Sussivari Frost Coven wove a misty citadel over Holberg.
n.The Marches: Henry Ward of Upwold was said to have paid the price demanded by Irra Harah, and Sadogua wished to speak privately with the three cleverest magicians of the Marches.
n.Thule: A penumbral veil was reportedly drawn over Urdur in Thule-held Otkodov, though it is unclear whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi are similarly veiled.
n.Urizen: Urizen fleets faced reduced trade, Redoubt and Morrow were veiled and fortified, and Morrow's veil resisted an attempt to steal its stars; Sadogua offered Urizen magicians mana and forged boons, and offered Nicassia the chance to have him devour parts of the Citadel Guard's cyclic magic.
n.Wintermark: Citadels rose over Kallavesa and Hahnmark, and Leviathan arranged for Tarqeq Icetongue and up to two Icewalkers to meet the mysterious Lake Dwellers linked to Sermersuaq.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Autumn magic that slowed Grendel pirates and sped Imperial ships faded as the Equinox approached, leaving traders exposed unless it is renewed.
t.Feroz: A penumbral veil drawn during the Summer Solstice warps the stars into a scrying-blocking shroud, bringing heavy dark fog.
t.Hahnmark: A frozen citadel of stone and ice was raised in Hahnmark's hills and mountains, protecting the land until the Autumn Equinox.
t.Holberg: The Sussivari Frost Coven wove mists over Holberg's marshes, raising a protective citadel until the Equinox.
t.Kahraman: A citadel of stone and ice was conjured in Kahraman's hills and mountains, offering safe haven while it stood.
t.Kallavesa: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a misty marsh citadel over Kallavesa that faded with the Autumn Equinox.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the stars were absent over Liathaven for much of 381YE.
t.Madruga: A ritual penumbral veil hides Madruga's stars from scrying and shrouds the territory in dark fog.
t.Morrow: Morrow is veiled and was fortified with a citadel; an attempt to steal its stars after the Summer Solstice failed against the Urizen veil, though naga there still feel the urge to secrecy.
t.Necropolis: A penumbral veil drawn over Necropolis interferes with scrying and brings heavy, dark fog.
t.Otkodov: A penumbral veil has reportedly been worked over Urdur, but whether the rest of Otkodov is veiled remains unclear without scrying.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt lies under a penumbral veil and also gained a citadel of stone and ice in its hills.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos fleets faced reduced trade as the Bay of Catazar protection faded, and a penumbral veil now shrouds the territory.
t.Segura: The Icy Maw curse brought a damp, maddening summer, halved mana production and ruined some minor regio, but also smoothed the post-earthquake magical disruption before fading by the Equinox.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's stars remain stolen under a magnitude-fifty Night shroud expected to last until near Winter 382YE, while citadels rose in its forests and hills.
t.Sermersuaq: Leviathan arranged for Tarqeq Icetongue to meet the Lake Dwellers, possibly connected to the drowned dead that once attacked the territory and its recent rising dead.
t.Spiral: A citadel of stone and ice was raised in the hills and mountains of Spiral.
t.Tassato: Tassato's fleets faced reduced trade production as the magic protecting them from Grendel pirates faded.
t.Temeschwar: A penumbral veil drawn during the Summer Solstice obscures Temeschwar's stars and blankets it in dark fog.
t.The Barrens: The stars remain missing over the Barrens, impeding scrying, with the shroud expected to last until shortly before Winter 382YE.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Henry Ward of Upwold is said to have paid the price for Irra Harah's bounty.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: it is unclear whether the penumbral veil over Urdur also lies over Verthandi.
t.Zenith: The stars vanished over Zenith before the Spring Equinox, and the shroud is expected to last until the Spring Equinox 383YE unless removed or reinforced.

r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: Mentioned in passing: it is not yet clear whether the penumbral veil also covers Nithoggir.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: it is not yet clear whether the penumbral veil also covers Sküld.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Merchants report the ritual Drawing the Penumbral Veil has been worked over Urdur, hindering scrying there.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: The Sherard Hunters infused Axmure's forests with Spring magic, raising a protective citadel until the Autumn Equinox.

Put on your war paint.d: The Footfall of the Beginning returned the Burning Falcon's banner, so the Freeborn assembly could pass competing mandates to rally kohan to a revived army. Either would cut its cost by 20 wains and 40 crowns, and the bolder one would grant the True Conviction quality. A third mandate would help the Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs seize mithril. None takes effect until the Senate approves the army. Serra Briante and Kahraman citizens offered 20 wains of mithril to the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills at 22 crowns each. Marcher and Dawnish mandates could let generals refine army qualities, though Dawn's would bar giving ground. Wintermark's would extend fight with honour to poison-using allies.

n.Dawn: A Dawn assembly mandate, in a general or witch-focused version, would bar Dawnish generals from the Give Ground and Cautious Advance orders for a year and offer them chances to refine army qualities at the Winter Solstice. The ban would become permanent if any general took up such a chance.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj invasion of Semmerholm was defeated and Dawn has invaded Ossium, and Wintermark likens poisoning and ambush tactics to Druj ways.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel have been forced out of Kahraman and their last soldiers rounded up in Madruga by Marcher armies.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are cited as having already reshaped their armies to suit their traditions over the past year.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the original Burning Falcon was lost to a Jotun invasion of Kallavesa, and the Jotun have since been driven from Kahraman.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr have reshaped their armies to fit their traditions, and Navarr armies helped drive the Grendel and Jotun from Kahraman.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly could rally kohan to revive the Burning Falcon, cheapening the army and possibly giving it True Conviction, and could urge its armies to plunder mithril. All of this depends on Senate approval of the new army.
n.The Marches: Marcher generals are celebrated for never giving ground. An assembly mandate would let them refine their armies' qualities at the Winter Solstice, with an emphasis on defending the land without drowning it in blood.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is cited as having already reshaped its armies to suit its traditions.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's generals have already made the Fist of the Mountain farsighted and the Green Shield truly heroic. A new mandate would extend fight with honour to allied armies using whatever it takes or fire in the blood.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Marcher armies are praised for driving back the vallorn to protect Bregasland.
t.Kahraman: Mine owners and traders of Kahraman joined Serra Briante in offering 20 wains of mithril toward a new Freeborn army, an offer open until the end of the Spring Equinox 383YE. Purchasing the mithril and then failing to raise the army would destroy the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills' standing there.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Burning Falcon was lost over 130 years ago defending Kallavesa against a Jotun invasion.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Marcher armies rounded up the last Grendel soldiers in Madruga.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Marcher generals are credited with liberating the Mournwold.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish invasion of Ossium is said to have cemented the nation's pride in its armies and generals.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish armies defeated the Druj invasion of Semmerholm before striking north.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Marcher armies fought the Jotun in defence of Sermersuaq.

r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: The people of Serra Briante, led by Loida i Drazia i Erigo's suggestion, offered 20 wains of mithril to the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills at 22 crowns a wain. The mithril can be bought once the Senate approves a new Freeborn army.

Silver clouds with grey linings.d: Sumaah declared peace but now looks to Timoj as the heart of the Way. Its orthodox missionaries, led by Lalok in Sanctuary, are denouncing the Synod, and preaching abroad led Limitu in Jarm to close the House of the Way. Nemoria is losing its war against rebel satrapies and still hires Imperial mercenaries. The Synod allowed a few carefully chosen Asaveans to train as priests. Faraden trade boosts Segura. The Iron Confederacy demands copies of the Empire's maps of its coast and warns about liao smuggling. The Commonwealth and the Sarcophan agreed to attend the slavery summit. Cargo was fortified, and over twenty-five captains crossed into the Mountains of the Moon.

n.Dawn: Faraden merchants want a trade enclave in central Astolat to reach Dawnish luxuries, and the Sarcophan Kruidenkenner guild is reportedly interested in warehouses in Dawn, though neither has yet happened.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their attack on Morrow is cited as proof that they could have devastated Cargo had they moved south instead of north.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: their territory of Spiral is used to locate the Mountains of the Moon, which lie to its east.
n.Highguard: The Sumaah no longer recognise the White City of Bastion as the heart of the Way, and their missionary leader Lalok has based himself in Sanctuary in Necropolis, where Sarcophan warehouses have also been completed.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants enter the Empire from the Jotun territory of Reinos.
n.The Brass Coast: Feroz's temple keeps Asavean trade favourable but is blamed by the Suranni for liao smuggling. Segura prospers from Faraden trade, and the Asavean architect Almodin waits in Yellow Chase with no progress on the Iron Qanat.
n.The League: Asavean merchants frequent Sarvos and Asavean travellers visit the Great Game in Temeschwar. Faraden traders route through Tassato, and the Kruidenkenner are reportedly interested in League warehouses.
n.The Marches: The Sarcophan Kruidenkenner guild is reportedly interested in establishing warehouses in the Marches, and Moonwater Hall serves as the Faraden model for new trade enclaves.
n.Urizen: Cargo in Redoubt has been fortified, protecting its embassies, docks and runeforge, though this is scant comfort to Morrow after the Druj attack. Asavean travellers are visiting the Spiral Sword.
n.Varushka: Faraden merchants hope for an enclave in Volodmartz, probably at Triosk, to reach Varushkan timber and ore. A Kruidenkenner representative will attend Varushkan Winter Markets, and Varushkan armies are stationed in Redoubt.
n.Wintermark: The Sarcophan Kruidenkenner have opened a second enclave in Ivarsgard and are reportedly interested in further warehouses in Wintermark.

t.Astolat: Faraden merchants would like a trade enclave in central Astolat, ideally at Laroc and Oldheart, though there has been no movement on it yet.
t.Bastion: The Sumaah Republic has formally declared that it no longer recognises the White City of Bastion as the heart of the Way.
t.Bay of Catazar: The Empire's recent mapping of the Bay has angered the Iron Confederacy, which demands copies of the maps. Sharing them would need a Senate motion costing 10 Thrones.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: it is not named directly; the page refers only to Sumaah missionaries arriving at ports along the Empire's southern coast.
t.Feroz: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull helps secure preferential Asavean trade, but the Suranni accuse Feroz of being a route for liao smuggling and threaten to act themselves.
t.Kalino: Its coast was mapped during the Imperial survey of the Bay, which the Suranni call espionage and for which they demand the maps and recompense.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: it is not named directly; the page refers only to Faraden interest in Varushkan timber and ore.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: news of the Druj attack on Morrow, and how badly its defenders fared, is cited to show what Cargo has been spared.
t.Mountains of the Moon: The delayed spy network was finally completed, and over twenty-five Imperial captains crossed into the mountains with the Penumbral Watcher. Their findings are not yet public, and Axou scouts apparently did not take part.
t.Necropolis: The Sarcophan warehouses here have been completed, and the Sumaah missionary leader Lalok is resident in the port town of Sanctuary.
t.Redoubt: Cargo, home to three embassies, has been fortified with Axou planning, Jarmish magic and Sarcophan materials, making it safer from orc invasion. Asavean travellers are also visiting the Spiral Sword.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: Faraden merchants pass through Reinos as they enter the Empire on their way to Segura.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Asavean merchants are common visitors to Sarvos.
t.Segura: The completed south-west road network has brought Faraden merchants and increased prosperity to Segura, their first port of call in the Empire.
t.Shavronne: Its coast was mapped during the Imperial survey of the Bay, prompting Suranni demands for the maps and recompense.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Mountains of the Moon are described as lying to the east of Zenith and Spiral.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Faraden traders reach Tassato along the Sunset roads before spreading out along the Blood Red Roads.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Asavean travellers have begun visiting the Great Game in Temeschwar.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: it is not named directly; the page cites Moonwater Hall as the model the Faraden want for new trade enclaves.
t.Veroigne: Its coast was mapped during the Imperial survey of the Bay, which the Suranni call spying and for which they demand the maps and recompense.
t.Volodmartz: Faraden merchant families hope to build a trade enclave in Volodmartz, most likely at Triosk, though nothing has happened yet.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Mountains of the Moon are described as lying to the east of Zenith and Spiral.

r.Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand: Lalok, Pilgrim of Courage, leader of the Sumaah missionaries, is staying at the Bright Destiny Inn in Sanctuary and welcomes visitors and messengers wishing to discuss the mission.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: The Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis has returned to his lodgings in Yellow Chase to oversee the Iron Qanat, but is concerned that no progress appears to be being made on it.

Starting at the end.d: Inspired by the Blood Red Roads, civil service engineers proposed several projects. The Iron Roads (200 wains of white granite, 400 crowns, one year) would expand roads across Karov, Miekarova and Volodmartz, boosting mines, forests and four Bourse resources. Wintermark's beacons (40 granite, 40 weirwood, 160 crowns) would make barbarian invasions of Hahnmark and Kallavesa contested and allow units to garrison them. The Marches were offered the Grand Western Highway, the Otterway and the Great Westward Canal. The Brass Coast was offered the Garden Roads in Feroz, a possible road into Kalino and the Cinnabar Roads, later withdrawn after Jotun damage. The beacons were completed before Spring 383YE, and the Iron Roads were later extended into Ossium.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Astolat and Semmerholm are listed among the territories the Blood Red Roads pass through.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Senate approved an expansion of the Iron Roads into Ossium in Spring 384YE.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the planned White Roads are cited as an ambitious project that would bring more pilgrims to Bastion and Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Imperial Orc traders are among those who regularly use the central road through Miekarova.
n.Jotun: Jotun invasions loom over the proposals: the beacons might have warned of their seizure of Sermersuaq, the Sermersuaq beacons await its liberation, and Jotun damage to Kahraman ended the Cinnabar Roads opportunity.
n.Navarr: Navarr traders stood to gain from roads into Kahraman and Miekarova, and surveyors sketched a protected route into Liathaven, though no work is possible while it lies outside the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn were offered the Garden Roads in Feroz, a possible trade road into Kalino, and the Cinnabar Roads in Kahraman, which were withdrawn after Jotun damage.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League's cities are linked by the Blood Red Roads, and the Iron Roads might bring more materials to Temeschwar's Assayer's Guild.
n.The Marches: The Marches were offered the Grand Western Highway, the Otterway and the Great Westward Canal to spread prosperity beyond Upwold to Mitwold, Mournwold and Bregasland.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a proposed Miekarova road would end at the Embassy to Otkodov.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's heliopticon is cited as a far grander counterpart to Wintermark's beacons.
n.Varushka: The Senate approved the Iron Roads in Autumn 383YE, bringing safer warded roads, ingots and materials to mine and forest owners, and greater output from four Varushkan Bourse resources.
n.Wintermark: Uninterested in new roads, the Winterfolk had their beacons and watchtowers in Hahnmark and Kallavesa approved in Autumn 382YE and completed before Spring 383YE.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the proposed White Roads would bring more pilgrims to the holy city of Bastion.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the White Roads would help traders on the south-eastern shores of the Bay reach the wider Empire.
t.Bregasland: Proposals included a highway spur to Graven Rock that would boost Bregasland's mines, and repairs to the Otterway causeway to enrich its farms; the Bregas angrily rejected any extension further into the Fens.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.
t.Feroz: The proposed Garden Roads would bring rings to Feroz businesses, herbs to its gardens and extra herbs to the Keeper of the Spice Gardens; a further road from Bramar towards Kalino was also suggested.
t.Hahnmark: Expanded beacons and watchtowers were approved and completed, making barbarian invasions of Hahnmark contested unless an enemy takes Kalpaheim.
t.Kahraman: The Cinnabar Roads would have enriched Kahraman's mines and businesses and raised Fort Braydon to a rank two fortification, but Jotun damage made the opportunity unavailable.
t.Kalino: A possible Sunlit Road from Bramar to Ruenda in Kalino would need negotiation by the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy and Confederate work on their side of the border.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's pilgrim trails were judged good enough, but its beacons and watchtowers were approved and completed, making barbarian invasions there contested while the Rundhal Marsh holds.
t.Karov: Under the Iron Roads, roads between Delev, Olvanshka and Kolvy would be maintained and expanded, and a new road would link Kolvy to Korotny along the Weirwater border.
t.Karsk: The Crow Roads of Karsk served as the template for the Iron Roads, which might in turn open easier access to Karsk's mines.
t.Liathaven: Surveyors could only make vague sketches of a protected route into Liathaven while it remains outside the Empire, though the Cinnabar Roads would have eased resettlement.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.
t.Miekarova: The Iron Roads would reinforce the Essk–Olodny–Mormyk road and add a new route to the Night Quarry, Wendell's Hope and the Embassy to Otkodov.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold would gain from a repaired Western Road through to Meade and Odd's End, or from a canal along the River Meade, with rings for its businesses and farms.
t.Mournwold: The highway or canal would reconnect the Mournwold to the north, bringing rings to farms and businesses and extra ingots to mines, with uncertain effects on contact with its ex-Jotun orcs.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the proposed White Roads would bring more pilgrims to the tombs of Necropolis.
t.Ossium: The Senate approved an expansion of the Iron Roads into Ossium in Spring 384YE.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: a new Miekarova road would end at the Embassy to Otkodov.
t.Segura: The Sunset Road already brings Segura prosperity through trade with the Faraden, and the Garden Roads would extend the Feroz highway into Segura to Anduz.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory the Blood Red Roads pass through.
t.Sermersuaq: Once Sermersuaq is liberated from the Jotun, a smaller beacon network could cover it for 25 wains each of white granite and weirwood and 100 crowns.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Red Roads run north from Tassato, and the proposed highway would end there.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: more materials reaching Temeschwar might allow the Assayer's Guild to expand.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's trade boom from the Blood Red Roads has made other Marchers grumble, and the canal might one day extend there.
t.Volodmartz: The Iron Roads would add a major new road from the foothills north of Triosk past the Hunt of Alderei the Fair to Void and Veltsgorsk.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: a new Karov road would run along the border with Weirwater.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: A highway spur to Graven Rock would open access to Gravenmarch's mineral riches, adding 25 ingots of production each season across Bregasland's mines.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The proposed Otterway repairs would widen and pave the raised causeway to Ottery.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: The Otterway would continue south to Sallow, though the Bregas rejected any extension further into the Fens.
r.Feroz/Afarjasse: The hakima of Afar politely but firmly refused any road linking their isolated settlement to Bramar and vowed to oppose one.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: The region would share in the Garden Roads' proposed maintenance and expansion of the Feroz road network.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: The withdrawn Cinnabar Roads would have run from Briante to Fort Braydon and better protected the Great Mine of Briante.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Cinnabar Roads would have extended Fort Braydon's protection to the Damatian Cliffs, and past trade with Beacon Point here was choked by bandit orcs.
r.Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh: The Kallavesa beacons would stop working if an enemy force took control of the Rundhal Marsh.
r.Karov/Kamienczka: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' expansion of Karov's network between Delev, Olvanshka and Kolvy and its isolated vales.
r.Karov/Malimorzi: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' expansion of Karov's network, including the new road from Kolvy to Korotny.
r.Karov/Skoremujac: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' improved access to Karov's lesser-known vales.
r.Liathaven/Beacon Point: Bandit orcs once strangled trade between Beacon Point and Serra Damata, and surveyors could only sketch a protected route while Liathaven remains outside the Empire.
r.Miekarova/Dupadealuri: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' reinforcement of Miekarova's central road and access to isolated vales, forests and mines.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads in Miekarova, including better access to the Eternal Shafts of Time and the Night Quarry.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' reinforced road linking Essk, Olodny and Mormyk.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: The Western Road to Meade and Odd's End, now fallen into disrepair, would be restored under the Grand Western Highway and could continue as the Otterway.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Grand Western Highway would be extended through the Chalkdowns to Sarcombe, which is being rebuilt.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: The highway would run east from Sarcombe across the Greensward to Tassato.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: The region would share in the Mournwold benefits of the proposed highway or canal, and the withdrawn Cinnabar Roads would have run north from Kahraman into the Mournwold.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Any future Sermersuaq beacon network would only work while Sealtoq was not in enemy hands.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: The region would benefit from the Iron Roads' ambitious new road through Volodmartz towards Void and Veltsgorsk.

Tested again and again.d: After Synod statements urged priests to use their Right of Witness at the Military Council, Tarrat of the Legion's Rookery proposed ten national chaplains with judgement powers over their nation's generals. Carabella di Sarvos revived a plan to strengthen the Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path, including a veto on Declarations of Concord that would need a constitutional motion. Vitruvia of Tabulos suggested a Virtuous Wayleave appointed by the Synod. Jereboam of Sanctuary proposed Synod appointment of ambassadors and stronger powers for the Chaplain Consular, and others suggested similar changes for the Auditor and Imperial Inquisitor. The Constitutional Court found none of these unconstitutional in principle. The Freeborn objection to Almodin Oktístis building the Iron Qanat had little effect, and the Zemress festival was declined.

n.Dawn: Viviane de Coeurdefer's Assembly of the Nine mandate called priests to witness the Military Council, and the Dawn National Assembly sent Odelina de Rondell to act as confessor to the Dawnish generals until the end of Autumn 383YE.
n.Highguard: Jereboam of Sanctuary proposed that the Synod appoint the Empire's ambassadors and that the Chaplain Consular gain powers of revocation and excommunication. He praised Accalon of Felix's Watch's handling of Sumaah, and Zephaniah of Felix's Watch, Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path, was named as seeking Synod guidance.
