n.Imperial Orcs: Tarrat, a veteran orc preacher at the Legion's Rookery, proposed national chaplains who would support and hold to account each nation's generals. Plans to assign an Imperial Wayleave to the orcs inspired Vitruvia's Virtuous Wayleave idea.
n.Navarr: The Navarr National Assembly backed the call for guides to attend the Military Council and nominated Neala as liaison between Navarr guides and their generals.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Assembly's objection to Almodin Oktístis building the Iron Qanat drew little support among the Freeborn, apart from the Zemress refugees. The Senate could commission the Qanat again without him, and a Freeborn mandate already bars Synod interference with the Temple in Oran.

t.Feroz: The Freeborn statement against idolatry appeared to attack the Asavean Temple in Oran. An earlier mandate of tolerance means the Synod cannot interfere with the temple without major changes in relations with Asavea.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: home of Jereboam of Sanctuary, who proposed Synod oversight of Imperial diplomacy.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: associated with the Urizen architect Vitruvia of Tabulos, who proposed a Virtuous Wayleave for the Synod.
t.Segura: The Iron Qanat to be built in Segura by the Asavean Almodin Oktístis was denounced by the Freeborn Assembly. Unless the Senate commissions it afresh without him, he remains free to adorn it with whatever imagery he wishes, provided it meets the specifications.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Legion's Rookery in Skarsind is where Tarrat, author of the chaplain proposal, teaches.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Temple in Oran, which welcomes dozens of Asavean visitors each season, remains protected from Synod interference by the earlier Freeborn mandate of tolerance.
r.Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand: Mentioned in passing: linked to Jereboam of Sanctuary, the young wayfarer behind the ambassadorial and Chaplain Consular proposals.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Mentioned in passing: linked to Vitruvia of Tabulos, the architect who proposed a Synod-appointed Virtuous Wayleave.

The arch of the door.d: Chancellor Lady Jaycinda Griffonsbane regretted the move, though relocating nearer the heart of the Empire had been discussed before the invasion. With the barbarians only weeks from the spire, the safety of the students forced the decision. The Academy no longer seeks liao donations, so the Dean of Pilgrims, created by Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold, saw donations dwindle. The civil service proposed two Senate options at no cost and without a commission. One was a Canterspire College of the Way as an Urizen national title with 8 liao and 16 Synod votes. The other was the Canterspire Trust, a ministry aiding sanctuary seekers, with Delilah of Felix's Watch suggested. Doing nothing left the title at 6 liao. Neither option was taken before the Winter Solstice.

n.Dawn: Dawn became the Academy's new home, with buildings near the Castle of Thorns secured and most of the staff already moving there.
n.Druj: The Druj invasion of Morrow, with the barbarians within a few weeks' march of Canterspire, forced the Academy to abandon the spire.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost the Academy from Canterspire and was offered a College of the Way there, which would have become a national title chosen by the Urizen national assembly. The opportunity lapsed unused.

t.Astolat: The Academy's new buildings near the Castle of Thorns became the destination for its relocated staff and charges.
t.Morrow: Canterspire in Morrow was vacated by the Academy as the Druj closed in, leaving its shrine and buildings open for possible reuse while their survival hung on the spire not falling.

The lives you love to lead.d: Bite, believed to be of Druj origin and smuggled in through Holberg, was linked to bravo violence in Temeschwar, Sarvos, Holberg and especially Tassato, but could be stamped out by next year. With a greater-majority statement of principle, the League assembly could have Empress Giselle moved from Temeschwar back to Sarvos: to her repaired tomb in Caricomare, or to Capodomus Cathedral for 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns, creating a Bishop of Capodomus. Her return would stiffen resistance to the Grendel for a year. Holberg's upper-city walls became the Empire's largest fortification. The Ilotari offered two leomarids in return for a Senate invitation to the summit against slavery.

n.Druj: Bite is widely believed to have originated among the Druj, and Holberg's newly completed walls stand as a bulwark against them on the eastern border.
n.Grendel: The Grendel sacked Sarvos in 380YE, attempting to loot Giselle's tomb and carrying off Teodore von Mestra's remains. If Giselle were restored to Sarvos, any Grendel invasion within a year would face stiff civilian resistance.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the question of interring Giselle in the Necropolis alongside other Thrones was noted as settled years ago.
n.The League: Bite fuelled bloody bravo clashes across all four League cities while the militia slowly gained ground. The League assembly was offered the chance to bring Giselle home to Sarvos and possibly have her recognised as an exemplar to inspire all four cities.

t.Holberg: Holberg was the route by which bite entered the Empire. The city also finished its immense new upper-city walls and expanded the Imperial Menagerie, which now drew greater tourist revenue.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Giselle is noted as one of the few Thrones not interred in the Necropolis, a matter settled years before.
t.Sarvos: Bite was linked to bravo violence here, and Sarvos was offered the return of Giselle to her old tomb or Capodomus Cathedral, which would inspire its people to resist Grendel invasion for a year.
t.Tassato: Outside Holberg, most smuggled bite was ending up in Tassato, where several clashes between bravo bands had turned bloody.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar held Giselle's widely criticised tomb. Moving her would reduce the Guardian of Giselle's Tomb to 6 votes and 3 liao, and the city also suffered bite-linked bravo violence.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Mentioned in passing: Holfried is not named, though the page's news of bite smuggling, the city walls and the Imperial Menagerie concerns Holberg generally.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer Park lay outside the new upper-city walls, but with such a fortification nearby it was considered hardly defenceless, despite some lower-city grumbling.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Giselle's repaired family tomb at Caricomare on Cigno could take her sarcophagus again at no extra cost, provided the Grendel did not conquer the island again.

The only reason that I sing.d: At the Summer Solstice 382YE the troubadours of Dawn named champions for all seven virtues for the first time in many years. They also named Odelina de Rondell champion of the Way, Ser Isidore Ossienne champion of Love and Colwyn de Rondell champion of Glory. A proposed Synod mandate, available only at the Autumn Equinox, would make the Love and Glory champions permanent. The weavers of Spiral Castle and Laroc would then craft a Troubadour's Ring and a Circlet of Command for them each year, though some fear heresy. Separately, the Senate created the Champion of Courage to bear Torchbrand, one of seven shields lost at Reikos in 367YE. Measure is held by a Jarmish magician-prince, and the Senate could create titles for the other six.

n.Dawn: Dawn's troubadours named a full slate of Summer champions, and the new champions of Love and Glory captured the imagination of nobles and yeofolk alike. The national assembly may now enact a mandate making these uniquely Dawnish champions permanent, despite concerns it may be heretical.
n.Druj: The Pilgrim's Shields were lost when their bearers fell before the Druj at Reikos in 367YE. The orcs may hold one or more of the missing shields, and their habit of using religious items to bait traps might be turned against them.
n.Grendel: Grendel is not named on the page, but it held Spiral, whose Spiral Castle weavers would craft a Troubadour's Ring each year for Dawn's Champion of Love if the mandate passes.
n.Highguard: The seven Pilgrim's Shields, including the Senate-recognised Torchbrand, were forged by Ezkiah the Benefactor, greatest smith of the Highborn in the Empire's early years. Their recovery would inspire the Empire's faithful.

t.Astolat: As Dawnish land, Astolat's nobles and yeofolk share in the enthusiasm for the new champions of Love and Glory. Dawnish weavers would craft regalia for these champions if the mandate is enacted.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the seven Pilgrim's Shields were lost when their bearers fell before the Druj at the battle of Reikos in 367YE.
t.Spiral: If the Dawnish mandate passes, the weavers of Spiral Castle would be inspired to create a Troubadour's Ring each year, delivered to the troubadours of Dawn for the Champion of Love.
t.Weirwater: As Dawnish land, Weirwater's people share in the national enthusiasm for the champions of Love and Glory. Dawnish weavers would craft regalia for these champions should the mandate be enacted.

The scars from tomorrow.d: A proposed Navarr mandate would set guides to challenge heresy among foreign trod-walkers. It would cost every Navarr congregation a rank and drive away Faraden merchants. Several trods briefly and strangely strengthened. In Liathaven, Wither the Seed began blighting all life for thirty years and slowing the vallorn, which extends the chance to cleanse Westwood until Summer 383YE, but wild Spring magic shredded its newly restored trods. Spring ritual magic linked to Yaw'nagrah pushed Brocéliande's vallorn into Boar's Dell and Elerael. Military units could defend Greenstead and Brackensong: 1,000 force saves Boar's Dell and 2,000 saves both. Llofir sought a parley about the vallorn.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's spread into Dawn's Astolat three years earlier is recalled as unlike the current Brocéliande advance.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their earlier withdrawal from Elerael and their rampage across Urizen are cited, as is the loss of Zenith's trods.
n.Highguard: Highborn pilgrims crowd the trods and are unlikely to accept Navarr guides lecturing them about the virtues. Llofir asked for a representative of the pilgrims at its parley on the vallorn.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: their hold on Liathaven blocks easy restoration of its trods, and their capture of Sermersuaq strains the Empire's armies.
n.Navarr: The nation faced a costly choice over policing the trods. It saw its Liathaven trod work undone, and its steadings in Boar's Dell and Elerael are threatened by a deliberately roused vallorn they must defend or abandon.
n.The League: The east-west trod through Foracci in Sarvos was one of the few routes where travellers noticed the trods briefly running faster and farther than normal.
n.The Marches: The trod through the market town of Sarcombe briefly strengthened, and Marcher Rucastle's support built Greenstead's stone walls, a rallying point for the defence of Boar's Dell.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Druj rampaging across Urizen is cited as a reason Imperial armies may not be spared for Brocéliande.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Sermersuaq to the Jotun is cited as straining the Empire and cutting into the trod network.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's expansion into Astolat three years ago is contrasted with the present advance, which shows no sign of spilling into neighbouring territories.
t.Brocéliande: Ritual Spring magic drawing on Yaw'nagrah has roused the vallorn here to creep into Boar's Dell and Elerael. The Empire must commit military force or abandon the Navarr footholds, possibly losing them entirely within about two years.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's expansion into Casinea three years ago is recalled as a different kind of event from the current spread.
t.Liathaven: The Wither the Seed curse began a thirty-year blight on all life here while lulling the vallorn back to sleep, but an intentional burst of Spring magic tore apart the newly restored trods to the vallorn's heart.
t.Mournwold: The trod through the market town of Sarcombe was one of those observed to strengthen briefly before the effect vanished.
t.Reikos: A green herald of Llofir crossed from Tamarbode into Elerael, bearing the eternal's request to parley about the vallorn.
t.Sarvos: The east-west trod through Foracci, though not the northern one, briefly carried travellers faster and farther than usual.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: no events are described here, though the territory is linked to the strengthened trod joining the Broch to Anvil.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: its loss to the Jotun is cited among the setbacks to the trod network and to Imperial strength.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story, the thief-taker picked up his quarry's trail after meeting an acquaintance in Tassato.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns dashed through the Barrens to reach Elerael after the Druj withdrew.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the loss of Zenith is noted as reducing, though not ending, the trods' draining of the vallorn.

r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: A few Navarr live at the Broch deep in the Black Boughs, and the trod joining the Broch to Anvil briefly strengthened.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: The vallorn's miasma, husks and ettercaps creep in and may claim a tenth of the region this season. Greenstead's stone walls offer a rallying point, and 1,000 effective force would hold the advance here.
r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns dashed through Dark Ranging to secure Elerael after the Druj withdrew.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: The vallorn's slow advance threatens its fragile new steadings and could take a tenth of the region this season. Brackensong Steading could anchor a defence, but holding Elerael as well as Boar's Dell requires 2,000 effective force. Llofir's herald also emerged here.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: very old vallornspawn husks come from Brocéliande, where Terunael itself once stood.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The curse has slowed the vallorn's recovery, so the chance to clear West Ranging lasts beyond the Winter Solstice, and its weakened vallornspawn may offer less resistance.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: The vallorn is slowly regaining strength here and will be fully restored by the Summer Solstice 383YE unless rooted out first. Scrying might reveal how much the curse has weakened its spawn.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: The trod through Sarcombe was one of the routes where travellers noticed a brief, unexplained strengthening.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: A green herald of the eternal Llofir crossed from Tamarbode into Elerael, carrying the request for a parley about the vallorn.
r.Sarvos/Foracci: The east-west trod through Foracci, but not the one running north, briefly let travellers walk faster and farther before the effect disappeared.

The way that the sunshine gleams.d: Several books sent to the library had carried hidden charms meant to leech knowledge, which instead destroyed it. Phaleron excised the corruption and reconsidered its purpose, choosing to protect and share knowledge rather than hoard it. Books sent by The Celestial Library will now be sealed and destroyed. A replacement ritual, Gift of Knowledge, was to be given to Archmage of Day Gancius della Notte di Sarvos. Phaleron asked the Conclave to seek a Senate-created Emissary of Phaleron title, offered a Declaration of Concord shielding the Anvil Library from hostile heralds, and said its herald Lioc would bring an arcane projection offering sanctuary to the people and books of Morrow and Zenith against the Druj.

n.Druj: The Druj conquest of Zenith and of many spires in Morrow, and their killing or enslavement of Urizeni scholars, has moved Phaleron close to wrath and prompted it to offer sanctuary against them.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the in-character story shows Myfanwy of Teeth Striding and representatives from Therunin's stridings and steadings helping Urizeni plan the evacuation of Canterspire.
n.Urizen: Phaleron's herald Lioc will meet Urizeni magicians at the Autumn Equinox with an arcane projection intended to offer sanctuary to the people of Morrow and Zenith and a refuge for their books and libraries.

t.Morrow: With many of Morrow's spires fallen to the Druj, Phaleron offers a potent arcane projection meant to give its people and libraries sanctuary from the invaders.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Myfanwy travels from Therunin, and representatives from almost every striding and steading of Therunin help with the Canterspire evacuation.
t.Zenith: Zenith's spires fell to the Druj before Morrow's, and Phaleron's offered projection is meant to provide sanctuary for its people and books against the Druj.

Think of the children.d: Cesare's statement passed 215–0, but the Mourn showed little enthusiasm, since Marcher friars traditionally find homes for orphans with relatives or charitable souls. Friar Margaret of Green March proposed converting the Jarl's Head, an abandoned inn in Sarcombe, into a register of births and deaths. The civil service offered three options: the register alone (6 wains of white granite, 12 crowns); the register plus shrines to the Little Mother across human settlements (40 wains, 80 crowns, yielding 900 rings a season to Mournwold Prosperity congregations); or the same including Jotun thrall settlements (50 wains, 100 crowns). Frederick di Sarvos offered to devote himself to any feat named by Viviane de Coeurdefer, provided the Assembly of the Nine upholds her judgement.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Viviane de Coeurdefer, Cardinal of Ambition, was challenged to submit a Statement of Endeavour to the Assembly of the Nine, with Frederick di Sarvos pledging to pursue any feat she names if it passes.
n.Jotun: Many new orphans of the war are Jotun, and one costlier option would extend the shrines and register to thrall settlements, signalling Imperial intent to incorporate the thralls into Marcher society; otherwise Jotun orphans would have to fend for themselves.
n.The League: The League's Cesare Enzo di Trivento drew on his nation's tradition of Little Mother orphanages to call for the great orphanage, while Holberg's Frederick di Sarvos was inspired to challenge the Cardinal of Ambition.
n.The Marches: Marchers largely rejected a grand orphanage as alien to their custom of placing orphans with kin, favouring instead the Sarcombe Register and possibly a network of Little Mother shrines across the Mourn.

t.Holberg: Frederick di Sarvos, a renowned architect holding a chair at the University of Holberg, offered to devote himself and rally fellow devotees of Ambition to whatever feat the Cardinal of Ambition names.
t.Mournwold: The Senate could build the Sarcombe Register in the town of Sarcombe, optionally with shrines to the Little Mother across the territory, providing 900 rings a season to its Prosperity congregations and possibly including Jotun thrall settlements.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story, an orphan's late father's estate was sold to a family moving back from Upwold.

r.Mournwold/Green March: Friar Margaret of Green March originated the register proposal, and the region is home to Hap the Soft, a Jotun thrall known for taking in dozens of orphans.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Mentioned in passing: Southmoor is not named directly, but lies within the Mournwold where the register and shrine network are proposed.

This might be your battle.d: Mazo i Zabala i Erigo's statement urging attacks around the Isle of Balsagoth caught on among the Freeborn, League, Highguard and some Urizen captains. The Grendel, overconfident after destroying the Freeborn Storm and the Atalaya shipyard, had an armada off Sarvos and privateers chasing Imperial merchants. Fleets could join "Attack the Slavers" and military units "Raid the Salt Mines". Total fleet strength would set the target, from Grendel shipping through the Temple of Tempest Jade, Vorlach, Balsagoth, up to Dubhtraig itself. Soldier strength would decide how many slaves were freed and how much was looted. Fleet Master Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra was expected to coordinate the raid. Freed slaves would gain sanctuary under Eska Crowspeaker's mandate.

n.Grendel: The Grendel faced a possible large Imperial raid on their shipping, the Temple of Tempest Jade, Vorlach, Balsagoth or Dubhtraig. Their slaves, mithril, weirwood and Salt Lords' prestige were all at risk, as was their ability to raise new navies and armies.
n.Highguard: The call to strike the slavers spread to Highguard. Its captains could join the raid, and freed slaves would likely be settled around the Bay of Catazar nations, Highguard among them.
n.The League: League captains embraced the call to raid the Broken Shore. The League was among the Bay of Catazar nations likely to receive liberated slaves.
n.Urizen: Some Urizen captains took up the call to attack the Grendel. Southern Urizen was named as a likely destination for slaves freed in the raid.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel believed they owned the bay, but Imperial fleets were invited to sail across it to strike the Broken Shore. The freed slaves would likely be brought to the nations around its shores.
t.Sarvos: A Grendel armada lay at anchor outside Sarvos, one the Empire could not match. The Grendel invasion of the city a year earlier was cited as reason to strike back at Dubhtraig.
t.Shayeel: The Grendel slave port and mining town of Vorlach on Shayeel's northern coast was a potential raid target if Imperial fleet strength reached 10,000. A strong enough attack could free up to 1,500 slaves, halt Salt Lord Moorvain's salt and mithril mines and leave lasting damage.

Trade all my tomorrows.d: A new road north of Mellfort, bypassing Hercynia's trods, eased the flow of metals west to Kalpaheim, while Steinr weapons, armour and jewellery spread outward. Building a Kalpaheim Trade Hall, which needed a Senate motion or wayleave, 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns, would connect Wintermark to the network, including cheap mana crystals from Thule. It might also send Wintermark weapons to Thule merchants serving their dragon masters. Mott of Fisher's Rock sent an apprentice with venomous weapons against vallornspawn. Llinos Fabledwing brought the Summer Acorn, said to come from Arden's Great Oak. Dhomiro Ximen i Suerta i Guerra sought backing for a stone casino in Cerevado, and Eli of the Seventh Step brought an ancient sun symbol.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the northern neighbours sharing the trade network's wealth, and as holders of a dedicated wayleave that Ximen i Suerta hoped to use.
n.Navarr: Navarr were part of the northern trade network. The Fabledwing Striding brought the Summer Acorn to Anvil, and Twyll Eternal, the Blackroot Broker, was asked to find buyers for Mott's venomous blades.
n.The Brass Coast: Dhomiro Ximen i Suerta i Guerra sought a wayleave, commission or Senate motion to build a great stone casino in Cerevado. He claimed it would bring prosperity to a town strained by poor refugees, after failing to win sponsorship from the Brass Coast's senators.
n.The League: Eastern metals had traditionally gone to Temeschwar first, but the new road diverted some trade west. Meanwhile Temeschwar developed a fashion for Steinr depictions of Varushkan Virtue-animals.
n.The Marches: Mott of Fisher's Rock, a reclusive Bregasland herbalist, sent an apprentice to Anvil with venomous weapons, surprising many by seeking a Navarr broker rather than a fellow Marcher.
n.Thule: Thule traders sold mana crystals cheaply into the northern trade network. There were fears that a Kalpaheim Trade Hall would let Wintermark weapons reach Thule merchants buying for their dragon masters.
n.Varushka: Varushkan miners and merchants such as Miloš of Delev drove the new trade, selling metals to Hahnmark's crafters and buying their weapons, armour and mail in return.
n.Wintermark: Steinr artisans profited from easier access to eastern metals. Wintermark could commission a Kalpaheim Trade Hall to join the northern trade network, at the risk of its weapons flowing to the Thule.

t.Bregasland: Mott of Fisher's Rock, a surly merrow herbalist living among marshspiders, dispatched an apprentice from Bregasland to sell venomous weapons at Anvil.
t.Hahnmark: Kalpaheim became the western end of a busier road from Delev, and a proposed Trade Hall there would require 16 wains of weirwood and 32 crowns and could be finished in a single season.
t.Hercynia: The new road to Kalpaheim bypassed Hercynia's rough trods, and the Fabledwing Striding had freed Hercynian villages from vallorn-infested mandowlas.
t.Otkodov: The Thule of Otkodov were part of the northern trade network, selling mana crystals cheaply, and might become buyers of Wintermark weapons if the Trade Hall were built.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar, traditionally the first destination for eastern metals, saw a growing fashion for Steinr portrayals of Virtue-animals. The Fabledwing had freed its village of Seraya Derevnya from plaguewulves.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Mott's name was a byword in the North Fens, and Greywater's eel-fishers reported her apprentice asking the quickest way to Anvil.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: Bont Goch, the village behind the Fabledwing Striding's founding, re-enchanted the Summer Acorn as a Coven Stone. The striding had also freed nearby Tyr Uchaf from vallorn-infested mandowlas.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Urdur was the point where Thule trade fed into the northern network, exchanging tempest jade for crystal mana that the network's members could buy cheaply.

Wages of sin.d: The Synod had condemned aiding Asavea, and the Imperatrix declared that crushing a slave rebellion debases the Empire. The Plenum still offered bounties well above the Imperial guerdon, and the law could not stop captains accepting. The Temple of the Way in Nemoria would act on one of two proposed mandates. One would call slaves to rise and join the rebels, risking a major international incident and the priests' safety. The other would urge Asaveans towards a peaceful, wise settlement, improving relations with Asavea. Bishop Henrietta von Holberg proposed a Vigilance mandate to list captains serving Asavea for the Imperatrix and the Cardinal. The Senate's only clear recourse was to abrogate the Temple's commission.

n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that the agreement which created the Temple in Nemoria also allowed the Asaveans to build their own temple in the Brass Coast.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Feroz is not named; the only link is the reference to the Asavean temple permitted in the Brass Coast under the agreement that founded the Temple in Nemoria.

We've been here forever.d: Eleonaris agreed to parley with Summer Archmage Solomon at a 7pm Friday reception in the Senate, where the Leonine Child would receive tribute. Her courtiers would then mingle across Anvil, on condition that no one asked for boons. Yaw'nagrah would meet Spring Archmage Fabienne Acoucher alone, saying the Empire could not be trusted to respect parley. Kaela offered Winter Archmage Emilia two non-military gifts. Ephisis declined a parley but sent traders to an open market. Azoth would receive Night Archmage Elyssiathain and give a gift to Ifan of the Darkwater Forge. Zakalwe offered to restore the Circlet of the Master Strategist but was puzzled by talk of a crystal crown lost in Brocéliande.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris praised the Golden Causeway proposed by the Lady of the Semmerlak, and Yaw'nagrah's message was delivered to a striding heading toward Ulvenholm.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Orrin, the Civil Service scribe who recorded Eleonaris's statement, is a Highguard scribe teased for 'Highborn nonsense'.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris cited the Empire's success in driving the Jotun out of Kahraman as one reason for her celebration.
n.Navarr: A small Navarr striding on the trod through Brocéliande was surrounded by handmaidens of the Green Mother. They were not attacked, and were made the bearers of Yaw'nagrah's demand to meet the Spring Archmage alone.
n.Urizen: Elyssiathain of Urizen, Archmage of Night, was to be received by Azoth for a formal parley. Zakalwe said he was pleased with how Urizen's magicians had used the Circlet of the Master Strategist and offered to restore its magic.

t.Brocéliande: Yaw'nagrah's handmaidens and a briar messenger stopped a Navarr striding in the vallorn-held forest, a reminder that the Conclave's enmity does not restrain eternals where the Empire does not hold sway. Zakalwe also denied knowing of any ancient crystal crown lost there.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr striding that met Yaw'nagrah's messenger was travelling toward Ulvenholm in Semmerholm.

r.Semmerholm/Ulvenholm: Mentioned in passing: Ulvenholm was the destination of the Navarr striding travelling north from Greenstead when Yaw'nagrah's handmaidens stopped it.

Words to make things right.d: After the Senate declared the Woods-that-fell Feni foreigners, diplomacy and trade cut the raiding but did not end it. The northern band left Southridge and headed north through Kalpamark. A Suaq grimnir, Kaukana, said he would speak for them at Anvil. In the Mournwold, the Marcher assembly's call to employ the southern band on farms failed. Some Feni now trade herbs for food instead, and the Alderly beater Dyl arranged for their representatives to meet the stewards. Neither band is hidden. An army ordered to do so could wipe them out for about fifty casualties, though not legally while they remain foreigners. An intercepted key would also let an army destroy the Alderly Feni this Autumn.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on this page, which deals with Feni troubles in Hahnmark and the Mournwold.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is listed among the territories where settlements were destroyed when the great sinkhole collapsed.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is listed among the territories where settlements were destroyed by the sinkhole that displaced the Feni.
n.The Marches: Marchers bore the brunt of the southern band's raids, and the assembly's call to employ the Feni as harvest workers failed, though dialogue reduced the raiding. Marcher stewards were invited to meet Feni representatives at Anvil, while Marcher armies could legally destroy the Alderly Feni this season.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's diplomacy through the Sentinel Gate helped reduce raids in Hahnmark, though the northern band refused further talks and moved north. Leaders of the Mark were told to expect the Suaq grimnir Kaukana at Anvil claiming to speak for the Feni.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on this page.
t.Hahnmark: The northern Woods-that-fell band, estimated at five hundred to eight hundred, raided halls and ambushed travellers on the roads to Kalpaheim before moving north. Any army there ordered to destroy them could break the band for about fifty casualties.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: settlements in Miaren were destroyed when the great sinkhole collapsed.
t.Mournwold: The southern band stayed camped on the Chalkdowns, raiding for food, though the Bounders' presence and herb trading reduced the harm. An army here could destroy both Feni bands, including the Alderly Feni before their wards change at the new year.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the grimnir Kaukana, who claims to speak for the Feni, hails from northern Sermersuaq.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: settlements in Temeschwar were destroyed when the great sinkhole collapsed.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the sinkhole destroyed settlements in Upwold, and the southern Feni band passed through it on its way to the Mournwold.

r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: The northern Feni band moved fast along the major trod running north-east through Kalpamark, avoiding Kalpaheim and the larger halls while raiding slightly more often.
r.Hahnmark/Southridge: The Woods-that-fell sheltered in Southridge's gullies over the Summer Solstice, ambushing travellers. Six weeks ago they left northward, joined by some local Feni.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: The insular Alderly Feni were left exposed by an intercepted key that would let an army destroy their hidden settlement for about 120 casualties, if done this Autumn. Meanwhile the Alderly beater Dyl arranged for Woods-that-fell representatives to come to Anvil.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The southern band camped on the Chalkdowns, raiding for food and livestock. Local farms' offers of harvest work failed, and ex-Jotun orc farms bought off the raiders with tribute.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: The people of Whittle formed a makeshift militia that lost no produce and drove off Feni raiders until they learned to avoid Whittle Hill.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Mentioned in passing: the Alderly Feni have occasionally raided Green March in the past.
